title: Separation logic proofs
description: Separation logic reasons about heaps with the separating conjunction: 'P * Q' means P and Q hold on disjoint memory. Frame reasoning lets proofs focus on the touched memory and ignore the rest — the logic that made verifying linked-list and tree code tractable, mechanized in tools like VeriFast.
method: Specify with pre/postconditions over heaplets; use the frame rule to ignore untouched memory; prove with symbolic execution over separation-logic assertions.
usage: Specify data-structure operations with heaplets; let the frame rule handle the untouched heap.

demo.code:
print('spec: {list(l)} reverse() {list(rev(l))}')
print('frame rule: rest of heap untouched -> proof local, scales')

title: Verified allocators
description: The allocator is the foundation: verified allocators (like the one in CompCert-adjacent work, or the verified malloc in the Ironclad project) prove that malloc/free never corrupt the heap. Proving the allocator sound means every program above it reasons about a correct heap.
method: Specify allocator invariants (free lists valid, no overlap); prove malloc/free preserve them; the proof covers the heap foundation.
usage: Use verified allocators for high-assurance systems; otherwise, fuzz and sanitize the allocator heavily.

demo.code:
print('verified malloc: free-list invariants proved')
print('all programs above reason about a correct heap')

title: Garbage collection as safety
description: GC is a memory-safety proof by construction: use-after-free and double-free are impossible when the collector owns deallocation. Managed runtimes (JVM, Go, .NET) trade deterministic timing for this guarantee — the oldest, most deployed memory-safety engine there is.
method: Collector traces reachability; frees only unreachable objects; the mutator can't corrupt the heap through deallocation.
usage: Prefer GC languages where pause times allow; the safety is structural, not per-program.

demo.code:
print('Go: object unreachable -> collected; no manual free exists')
print('use-after-free: IMPOSSIBLE by construction')

title: Miri undefined-behavior detection
description: Miri interprets Rust's mid-level IR with full UB checking — data races, invalid aliasing (Stacked Borrows), uninitialized reads — catching undefined behavior in unsafe code that the borrowck can't see. Unsafe Rust is verified by Miri the way safe Rust is verified by borrowck.
method: Run tests under Miri; it checks every operation against the operational semantics; UB reports pinpoint the violation.
usage: Run Miri on all unsafe code in CI; treat Miri failures as soundness bugs.

demo.code:
print('Miri: stacked-borrows violation at line 120')
print('invalid mutable aliasing in unsafe block -> UB confirmed, fix required')

title: CHERI capabilities
description: CHERI replaces raw pointers with hardware capabilities — pointers carrying bounds, permissions, and validity that the hardware enforces on every access. Buffer overflows and control-flow hijacks trap in hardware. It's memory safety as architecture, proved down to the ISA.
method: Capabilities in registers/memory; monotonicity (can't forge or widen); hardware checks per dereference; compartmentalization built in.
usage: Target CHERI platforms for high-assurance deployments; compartmentalize with capabilities.

demo.code:
print('capability: bounds [0x1000,0x1100), perms RW')
print('access 0x1200 -> hardware trap (bounds violated)')

title: Fuzzing + sanitizers pipeline
description: The pragmatic memory-safety engine: coverage-guided fuzzing under ASan/UBSan/MSan, running continuously. Google's OSS-Fuzz found tens of thousands of memory bugs this way. It's not a proof, but as an ongoing bug-finding operation it complements provers — find the bugs fast, prove the critical paths.
method: Fuzz harnesses per parser/entry point; run under all sanitizers; triage crashes; add regression tests; keep fuzzing continuously.
usage: Fuzz every input parser continuously; combine all three sanitizers; never close a crash without a regression test.

demo.code:
print('fuzz target parse_packet: 48h, ASan+UBSan')
print('3 heap overflows found -> fixed -> regression tests added')

title: Shape analysis for heap structures
description: Shape analysis abstracts the heap into shape graphs — 'this region is a null-terminated singly-linked list' — and proves operations preserve the shape. TVLA pioneered it; modern analyzers prove list/tree manipulations memory-safe without annotations, handling the aliasing that defeats simpler analyses.
method: Abstract heap as shape graphs with summary nodes; transfer functions update shapes; prove dereferences always hit allocated nodes.
usage: Apply to container and data-structure code; let the analyzer discover the shapes.

demo.code:
print('shape: region R is null-terminated list')
print('insert(): shape preserved, all derefs allocated -> SAFE')

title: Bounds-checking instrumentation
description: Hardware and compiler bounds checking (Intel MPX historically, ARM MTE now, SoftBound+CETS) enforce spatial and temporal safety at runtime: every pointer carries bounds, every dereference is checked. MTE's tagged memory catches overflows in production with low overhead — enforcement as the proof's runtime twin.
method: Tag memory and pointers; check tags/bounds on access; violations trap; deploy on capable hardware for production protection.
usage: Enable MTE/CHERI where hardware allows; treat traps as security events, not just bugs.

demo.code:
print('MTE: pointer tag 0x3, memory tag 0x7 -> MISMATCH')
print('trap: buffer overflow stopped before corruption')
